headline.scope_text: The headline counts every work type of this reform, including units the Building Permits Survey may leave out (uncertain classifications and conversions). The record 'comparable' beside it is the survey-definition effect; the difference, drawn per draw, is 'headline_minus_comparable'.
headline.what: added units authorized by building permit, 2027-2031, state

rows.title: ADUs with a budget-capped state grant program (illustrative $20 million, $25,000 awards)
rows.reason: With a fixed appropriation, how many owners are served, how many additional ADUs are authorized in 2027-2031 beyond those who would build anyway, and at what net public cost?

rows.title: ADUs with a budget-capped state loan program (illustrative $20 million, $25,000 loans)
rows.reason: The same capped program paid as loans: how many additional ADUs, and what is the net public cost once repayments and losses are counted?

rows.title: ADUs with predictable approval, projects conserved over an extended horizon
rows.reason: If the slowest ADU reviews got faster, how many permits move into 2027-2031, and do all projects still show up once later years are counted?

rows.title: ADUs with predictable approval (slow reviews pulled to the median)
rows.reason: If the slowest ADU reviews got faster, how many permits move into 2027-2031?

rows.title: ADU benchmark worked out with the hazard on surviving sites (method check)
rows.reason: How much does the benchmark move when take-up uses up a finite stock of eligible sites and permits follow applications after a lag?

rows.title: ADUs with the zoning-district reading in the sample (Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Frankstown)
rows.reason: If, in the three sample jurisdictions, the already-legal share comes from their zoning districts (verified code text only: known by right, conditions relaxed, newly eligible, discretionary, unresolved at the statewide range) instead of the benchmark's share, how many ADUs does the benchmark add?

rows.title: ADUs with the zoning-district reading, counting Philadelphia's 2022 ADU checklist (guidance, a sensitivity)
rows.reason: The same zoning-district reading, but also counting the City of Philadelphia's own ADU checklist (guidance, not the code): how many ADUs does the benchmark add?

rows.title: Census-comparable scope (work types the permit survey counts)
rows.reason: Counts only added units of work types the Building Permits Survey counts as new units; additions, conversions and uncertain attached units are left out.

rows.title: ADUs with tight homeowner financing
rows.reason: How many fewer ADUs if owners can borrow less, at a higher rate?

rows.title: ADUs with easy homeowner financing
rows.reason: How many more ADUs if owners can borrow nearly all of the cost near the mortgage rate?

rows.title: ADUs at full installed cost (own meters, service upgrades)
rows.reason: What if every ADU needs a new electric service, its own utility laterals and new-home tap fees?

rows.title: ADUs with homeowner financing access (state program + counted rent)
rows.reason: If a state program pays part of the owner's cash share and lenders count part of the ADU's rent, how many more ADUs become feasible?

rows.title: ADUs with predictable approval and financing access
rows.reason: With both levers on the same draws: how many authorizations move into 2027-2031, and how many are newly feasible?

rows.title: Screened for practical capacity (sewer, flood zone, steep slope)
rows.reason: Removes added homes on land without public sewer, in the flood zone or on steep slopes; the joint bounds show the middle when the screens overlap fully or not at all.

rows.title: Project choice on shared lots (five-reform package)
rows.reason: Each shared lot goes once to the use that pays most (an ADU, a 2-6 unit building, a new house or no change); this is the reform's part of the package.

rows.title: Project choice and a building-capacity limit (five-reform package)
rows.reason: As project choice, and each area's yearly building is capped near its past peak; homes over the cap move past 2031.

rows.title: Correlated high cost, tight credit and slow review
rows.reason: One shared factor per draw moves costs, credit, review speed and the baseline's cycle together (each input keeps its own values, only their order across draws changes); the change per draw therefore also carries that reordering.
